commit_message:
[Torch] Register RestructureNonConstantAxes in the Torch input pipeline (#25041)

The torch-to-iree input pipeline did not schedule
RestructureNonConstantAxes,
so ONNX reductions with a runtime axes tensor kept a runtime `dim` and
failed
to legalize in ConvertTorchToLinalg with:
> failed to legalize operation 'torch.aten.sum.dim_IntList'

Although the pass is registered and visible in `iree-opt -help`, it was
never
run by default `iree-compile`. This schedules it before
ConvertTorchToTMTensor
so runtime single-element reduction axes (keepdims=1) are statically
resolved
and lower cleanly to linalg.

Also adds a lit smoke test running the full torch-to-iree pipeline to
guard the
pass stays scheduled, and updates the onnx_ops cpu_llvm_sync O0/O2 xfail
configs.

Fixes 28 reduce cases(improving onnx_ops pass counts: 864 -> 892 passed
(O0), 893 passed (O2)).

commit_message:
[Torch] Register RestructureNonConstantAxes in the Torch input pipeline (#25041)

The torch-to-iree input pipeline did not schedule
RestructureNonConstantAxes,
so ONNX reductions with a runtime axes tensor kept a runtime `dim` and
failed
to legalize in ConvertTorchToLinalg with:
> failed to legalize operation 'torch.aten.sum.dim_IntList'

Although the pass is registered and visible in `iree-opt -help`, it was
never
run by default `iree-compile`. This schedules it before
ConvertTorchToTMTensor
so runtime single-element reduction axes (keepdims=1) are statically
resolved
and lower cleanly to linalg.

Also adds a lit smoke test running the full torch-to-iree pipeline to
guard the
pass stays scheduled, and updates the onnx_ops cpu_llvm_sync O0/O2 xfail
configs.

Fixes 28 reduce cases(improving onnx_ops pass counts: 864 -> 892 passed
(O0), 893 passed (O2)).

Part of iree-org/iree#24378

commit_message:
[Flow] Retain nested executable pass manager by reference (#25160)

Executable canonicalization and CSE were added to a copy of the nested
pass manager, so they were discarded before the Flow pipeline ran. Keep
the manager owned by the pipeline so executable canonicalization and
common-subexpression elimination actually run and appear in the
serialized pipeline.

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Write embedded executable object data before linking (#25117)

The LLVMCPU pipeline did not serialize inline executable object data
into the temporary file passed to the linker, which then crashed on this
empty file.

Adds a lit test that exercises this path, by attaching a linker script
referencing `iree_hal_executable_library_query` as the inline data (to
avoid binary data).

```mlir
#hal.executable.object<{
    path = "object.o",
    data = "HIDDEN(object_fn = iree_hal_executable_library_query);"
}>
```

Adds a missing null check and drops a redundant file `flush` followed by
a `close` in the same source file.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

---------

commit_message:
[Runtime] Fix shift-count-overflow in next_power_of_two on 32-bit targets (#25142)

On 32-bit targets, iree_host_size_t and iree_device_size_t are only 32
bits wide. The `value |= value >> 32;` statement in
iree_host_size_next_power_of_two() and
iree_device_size_next_power_of_two() then fails to compile with
-Werror=shift-count-overflow. This happens even though the code is
inside an `if (sizeof(...) == 8)` branch that never runs on those
targets: the compiler still checks it.

This change splits the 32-bit shift into two 16-bit shifts, `(value >>
16) >> 16`. The result is the same on 64-bit targets, and no shift is
ever as wide as the type on 32-bit targets, so the warning goes away.

Fixes #25134

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Moritz Riesterer <moritz.riesterer@nxp.com>
name: setup / setup

[Vulkan] Trim replay cache binding table tests

because those commands already bypass the cache for their descriptor sets,
and the dispatch plus copy test, which the copy test and the existing
republication test already cover. Use the fixture's ReadBufferData and
detect a stale replay from the untouched new target instead of zeroing the
old one.

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert torchao affine quantization to LinalgExt (#25104)

Converts the typed torchao `quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine` ops
to `iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine`, reusing the
PT2E conversion. Ops whose parameters LinalgExt cannot index fall back
to Torch-to-Linalg. This also fixes PT2E per-channel-group ops with
flattened scales, which produced invalid IR. Also drops two unused
includes from `LinalgExtOps.cpp`.

Part of #24862.

[Torch] Convert torchao affine quantization to LinalgExt (#25104)

Converts the typed torchao `quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine` ops
to `iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine`, reusing the
PT2E conversion. Ops whose parameters LinalgExt cannot index fall back
to Torch-to-Linalg. This also fixes PT2E per-channel-group ops with
flattened scales, which produced invalid IR. Also drops two unused
includes from `LinalgExtOps.cpp`.

commit_message:
[Torch] Register RestructureNonConstantAxes in the Torch input pipeline (#25041)

The torch-to-iree input pipeline did not schedule
RestructureNonConstantAxes,
so ONNX reductions with a runtime axes tensor kept a runtime `dim` and
failed
to legalize in ConvertTorchToLinalg with:
> failed to legalize operation 'torch.aten.sum.dim_IntList'

Although the pass is registered and visible in `iree-opt -help`, it was
never
run by default `iree-compile`. This schedules it before
ConvertTorchToTMTensor
so runtime single-element reduction axes (keepdims=1) are statically
resolved
and lower cleanly to linalg.

Also adds a lit smoke test running the full torch-to-iree pipeline to
guard the
pass stays scheduled, and updates the onnx_ops cpu_llvm_sync O0/O2 xfail
configs.

Fixes 28 reduce cases(improving onnx_ops pass counts: 864 -> 892 passed
(O0), 893 passed (O2)).

Part of iree-org/iree#24378

Assisted-by: Claude Code, Doubao, DeepSeek

commit_message:
[Flow] Retain nested executable pass manager by reference (#25160)

Executable canonicalization and CSE were added to a copy of the nested
pass manager, so they were discarded before the Flow pipeline ran. Keep
the manager owned by the pipeline so executable canonicalization and
common-subexpression elimination actually run and appear in the
serialized pipeline.

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex

Signed-off-by: Christopher McGirr <mcgirr@roofline.ai>

[Flow] Retain nested executable pass manager by reference (#25160)

Executable canonicalization and CSE were added to a copy of the nested
pass manager, so they were discarded before the Flow pipeline ran. Keep
the manager owned by the pipeline so executable canonicalization and
common-subexpression elimination actually run and appear in the
serialized pipeline.

commit_message:
[Torch] Register RestructureNonConstantAxes in the Torch input pipeline (#25041)

The torch-to-iree input pipeline did not schedule
RestructureNonConstantAxes,
so ONNX reductions with a runtime axes tensor kept a runtime `dim` and
failed
to legalize in ConvertTorchToLinalg with:
> failed to legalize operation 'torch.aten.sum.dim_IntList'

Although the pass is registered and visible in `iree-opt -help`, it was
never
run by default `iree-compile`. This schedules it before
ConvertTorchToTMTensor
so runtime single-element reduction axes (keepdims=1) are statically
resolved
and lower cleanly to linalg.

Also adds a lit smoke test running the full torch-to-iree pipeline to
guard the
pass stays scheduled, and updates the onnx_ops cpu_llvm_sync O0/O2 xfail
configs.

Fixes 28 reduce cases(improving onnx_ops pass counts: 864 -> 892 passed
(O0), 893 passed (O2)).

commit_message:
Bump cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0 in the github-actions group (#25175) Bumps the github-actions group with 1 update: [cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action](https://github.com/cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action). Updates `cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action` from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action's releases.

v2.24.0

Behavior changes

  • ignore: build now only skips build/ at the repo root. Earlier versions also skipped nested folders such as src/build/, which was a bug. To skip every build folder, use ignore: '**/build'.
  • A relative database path is now resolved against the workspace (the working directory), not against repo-root. repo-root must be inside the workspace.
  • When the action downloads clang-format or clang-tidy (on Windows, or when the runner doesn't have the requested version), it now gets the newest patch release of that major version (for example, 14.0.6 instead of 14.0.0), together with clang's resource headers.

Improvements

  • windows-11-arm runners work now: cpp-linter no longer depends on pygit2, which has no Windows arm64 wheel.
  • A repo-root that is a sub-folder of the git repository works now.
  • Comments and reviews are posted through git-bot-feedback, which fixes the API URLs on GitHub Enterprise Server.

Bump cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0 in the github-actions group (#25175) Bumps the github-actions group with 1 update: [cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action](https://github.com/cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action). Updates `cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action` from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action's releases.

v2.24.0

Behavior changes

  • ignore: build now only skips build/ at the repo root. Earlier versions also skipped nested folders such as src/build/, which was a bug. To skip every build folder, use ignore: '**/build'.
  • A relative database path is now resolved against the workspace (the working directory), not against repo-root. repo-root must be inside the workspace.
  • When the action downloads clang-format or clang-tidy (on Windows, or when the runner doesn't have the requested version), it now gets the newest patch release of that major version (for example, 14.0.6 instead of 14.0.0), together with clang's resource headers.

Improvements

  • windows-11-arm runners work now: cpp-linter no longer depends on pygit2, which has no Windows arm64 wheel.
  • A repo-root that is a sub-folder of the git repository works now.
  • Comments and reviews are posted through git-bot-feedback, which fixes the API URLs on GitHub Enterprise Server.

🐛 Bug fixes

  • fix: pass action inputs to run steps through env by @​shenxianpeng in #508

📝 Documentation updates

Sourced from cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action's releases.

v2.24.0

Behavior changes

  • ignore: build now only skips build/ at the repo root. Earlier versions also skipped nested folders such as src/build/, which was a bug. To skip every build folder, use ignore: '**/build'.
  • A relative database path is now resolved against the workspace (the working directory), not against repo-root. repo-root must be inside the workspace.

Bump cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0 in the github-actions group (#25175) Bumps the github-actions group with 1 update: [cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action](https://github.com/cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action). Updates `cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action` from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action's releases.

v2.24.0

Behavior changes

  • ignore: build now only skips build/ at the repo root. Earlier versions also skipped nested folders such as src/build/, which was a bug. To skip every build folder, use ignore: '**/build'.
  • A relative database path is now resolved against the workspace (the working directory), not against repo-root. repo-root must be inside the workspace.
  • When the action downloads clang-format or clang-tidy (on Windows, or when the runner doesn't have the requested version), it now gets the newest patch release of that major version (for example, 14.0.6 instead of 14.0.0), together with clang's resource headers.

Improvements

  • windows-11-arm runners work now: cpp-linter no longer depends on pygit2, which has no Windows arm64 wheel.
  • A repo-root that is a sub-folder of the git repository works now.
  • Comments and reviews are posted through git-bot-feedback, which fixes the API URLs on GitHub Enterprise Server.

🐛 Bug fixes

  • fix: pass action inputs to run steps through env by @​shenxianpeng in #508

Bump cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0 in the github-actions group (#25175) Bumps the github-actions group with 1 update: [cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action](https://github.com/cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action). Updates `cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action` from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action's releases.

v2.24.0

Behavior changes

  • ignore: build now only skips build/ at the repo root. Earlier versions also skipped nested folders such as src/build/, which was a bug. To skip every build folder, use ignore: '**/build'.
  • A relative database path is now resolved against the workspace (the working directory), not against repo-root. repo-root must be inside the workspace.
  • When the action downloads clang-format or clang-tidy (on Windows, or when the runner doesn't have the requested version), it now gets the newest patch release of that major version (for example, 14.0.6 instead of 14.0.0), together with clang's resource headers.

Improvements

  • windows-11-arm runners work now: cpp-linter no longer depends on pygit2, which has no Windows arm64 wheel.
  • A repo-root that is a sub-folder of the git repository works now.
  • Comments and reviews are posted through git-bot-feedback, which fixes the API URLs on GitHub Enterprise Server.

🐛 Bug fixes

  • fix: pass action inputs to run steps through env by @​shenxianpeng in #508

📝 Documentation updates

Bump cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0 in the github-actions group (#25175) Bumps the github-actions group with 1 update: [cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action](https://github.com/cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action). Updates `cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action` from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action's releases.

v2.24.0

Behavior changes

  • ignore: build now only skips build/ at the repo root. Earlier versions also skipped nested folders such as src/build/, which was a bug. To skip every build folder, use ignore: '**/build'.
  • A relative database path is now resolved against the workspace (the working directory), not against repo-root. repo-root must be inside the workspace.
  • When the action downloads clang-format or clang-tidy (on Windows, or when the runner doesn't have the requested version), it now gets the newest patch release of that major version (for example, 14.0.6 instead of 14.0.0), together with clang's resource headers.

Improvements

  • windows-11-arm runners work now: cpp-linter no longer depends on pygit2, which has no Windows arm64 wheel.

commit_message:
[Vulkan] Trim replay cache binding table tests

Drop the fill and update test, which never reaches the binding table check
because those commands already bypass the cache for their descriptor sets,
and the dispatch plus copy test, which the copy test and the existing
republication test already cover. Use the fixture's ReadBufferData and
detect a stale replay from the untouched new target instead of zeroing the

[Vulkan] Trim replay cache binding table tests

Drop the fill and update test, which never reaches the binding table check
because those commands already bypass the cache for their descriptor sets,
and the dispatch plus copy test, which the copy test and the existing
republication test already cover. Use the fixture's ReadBufferData and
detect a stale replay from the untouched new target instead of zeroing the
old one.

commit_message:
[Runtime] Fix shift-count-overflow in next_power_of_two on 32-bit targets (#25142)

On 32-bit targets, iree_host_size_t and iree_device_size_t are only 32
bits wide. The `value |= value >> 32;` statement in
iree_host_size_next_power_of_two() and
iree_device_size_next_power_of_two() then fails to compile with
-Werror=shift-count-overflow. This happens even though the code is
inside an `if (sizeof(...) == 8)` branch that never runs on those
targets: the compiler still checks it.

This change splits the 32-bit shift into two 16-bit shifts, `(value >>
16) >> 16`. The result is the same on 64-bit targets, and no shift is
ever as wide as the type on 32-bit targets, so the warning goes away.

Fixes #25134

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Moritz Riesterer <moritz.riesterer@nxp.com>
name: Test AMD R9700 / test_r9700

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Write embedded executable object data before linking (#25117)

The LLVMCPU pipeline did not serialize inline executable object data
into the temporary file passed to the linker, which then crashed on this
empty file.

Adds a lit test that exercises this path, by attaching a linker script
referencing `iree_hal_executable_library_query` as the inline data (to
avoid binary data).

```mlir
#hal.executable.object<{
    path = "object.o",
    data = "HIDDEN(object_fn = iree_hal_executable_library_query);"
}>
```

Adds a missing null check and drops a redundant file `flush` followed by
a `close` in the same source file.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

---------

Signed-off-by: Romain Paquet <rpaquet@kalrayinc.com>
name: runtime :: windows-2022

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Write embedded executable object data before linking (#25117)

The LLVMCPU pipeline did not serialize inline executable object data
into the temporary file passed to the linker, which then crashed on this
empty file.

Adds a lit test that exercises this path, by attaching a linker script
referencing `iree_hal_executable_library_query` as the inline data (to
avoid binary data).

```mlir
#hal.executable.object<{
    path = "object.o",
    data = "HIDDEN(object_fn = iree_hal_executable_library_query);"
}>
```

Adds a missing null check and drops a redundant file `flush` followed by
a `close` in the same source file.

commit_message:
[Python] Support 32-bit host pointers in DLPack export (#25164)

the pointer-size assertion rejects a 32-bit host even when the exported
address fits. Replace it with a runtime check that the address plus
